premise: At 60, after 27 years as a school custodian, I returned to care for my dying mother, who left me 70% of her 1950s seaside carousel and snack pavilion worth $640,000, but my sister-in-law forged a codicil cutting me out and sold the property to a regional amusement chain for $910,000, mailing me a $4,800 cotton-candy check; I found Mom's original will inside the hollow carved-mane horse she always painted, voided the sale, and now run 'Spindle of Deceit Carousel,' where she waxes brass poles in a smock that says 'Painted Over My Inheritance' and every ride ticket prints her probate-fraud docket.
